title: Knowledge check: SQLite Database Files and Connection Types

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies to “SQLite Database Files and Connection Types”?
options: Rely on undocumented behavior and skip checking the actual SQLite runtime.
Concatenate untrusted input directly into SQL and suppress errors.
Assume the result is correct without checking the schema, data or expected output.
Inspect the schema and actual stored values rather than assuming declared column types enforce rigid typing.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the schema and actual stored values rather than assuming declared column types enforce rigid typing.
questions.explanation: SQLite Database Files and Connection Types: Inspect the schema and actual stored values rather than assuming declared column types enforce rigid typing. SQLite has five storage classes and type affinity; use STRICT tables where they fit and validate data intentionally.

questions.answer_key: Reduce it to a reproducible fixture, inspect schema and values, and verify the expected result.
questions.explanation: A controlled fixture helps isolate behavior and makes the test repeatable. Preserve constraints and state the assumptions you verified.

questions.prompt: What should be recorded before depending on an SQLite capability related to “SQLite Database Files and Connection Types”?
